Source: @sahandiranmehr

A member of the Israeli delegation is writing down the names of those who walked out of Netanyahu's speech! The United Nations was founded after the Second World War. Poor humanity, after all that bloodshed, came slightly to its senses and said to itself: Surely from now on we'll settle things through dialogue and diplomacy and sitting around a table — not with bombs and cannons and tanks. In short, they wanted to make the world understand that human beings, if they are human beings, can use a tongue instead of teeth, and logic instead of "oldorm and boldorm"! Now, however, Trump the American — who all this time was showing off the free world and democracy and human rights, and whose predecessors brought down the Iron Curtain with that same bluster — conjures hell before everyone's eyes from behind the podium, saying that if they don't listen to him he can annihilate an entire nation; Netanyahu hoists the pagers like a trophy of honor and tells his critics: "Coward" — and the most interesting scene of all is this: him imagining himself as the monitor and snitch of Khan Bala, ruler and cherry switch in hand, waiting to hand over to His Excellency the list of names of those who didn't sit at the master's whipping post and left the session, so he can light the pipe of the "bad ones."
@sahandiranmehr

entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @sahandiranmehr

Unless "always," "attack," and "my country" mean something else entirely, then Your Majesty, allow me to point out that your child has "always" been in favor of "attacking" "your country." Unless — God forbid — you're like Eshrat Khanom, our childhood neighbor, who whenever the neighbors complained about her child causing trouble, would say: "I'm just as fed up as you are." And when the neighbors said, "Then kindly pay for the damage from his fire-setting?" she'd say: "I'm fed up myself — why should I pay for that unruly brat?" And when the neighbors said, "Then at least since you're his mother, twist his ear," she'd say: "Now for the sake of a bottle, I should rip my child's liver out like the man-eating Hind?!" And finally, when they said, "How is it you say nothing to him and yet claim you're fed up too?" she'd say: "A person should turn into a dog before becoming a mother, rather than feed people this nonsense!"@sahandiranmehr

The panel examined the logic behind the war's continuation and its end along three main axes: "Iran's reaction to UN Security Council Resolution 479," "the period of the liberation of Khorramshahr and why the fighting continued," and "the turning point from the capture of Faw to the acceptance of Resolution 598."Sahand Iranmehr, international relations researcher:▫️To put it very briefly, Resolution 598 was in fact an "accumulation of crises"; when this resolution was first proposed to Iran, Iran did not accept it, but at the same time it did not reject it either; and that same state of ambiguity existed: neither full acceptance nor full rejection. From Pen to Power: The Hard Path of Proving One's Worth

In the Middle Ages, secretaries were the ones who had to commit the word of power to paper—a vital profession whose traces are scattered throughout our history. A world woven from threats, crises, and, of course, intelligence and cunning.

In "Chahar Maqaleh" by Nezami Aruzi, the story of Askafi offers a glimpse into this very world. A man who went largely unnoticed in one administration, yet when he moved elsewhere, the very skills he possessed suddenly gained value—and he rose with them.

In this episode, we'll use this same story as a starting point to explore topics like meritocracy, political rationality, and the like.

Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @sahandiranmehr

Sahand Iranmehr - Although the division between Bedouin and city-dweller in the case of Ansarullah - Saudi Arabia (and its satellites) is not very precise, in terms of unequal welfare and resources, my angle of view unconsciously ties to Ibn Khaldun's "Muqaddimah":
"City-dwellers have grown accustomed to comfort and prosperity. They have entrusted the defense of their lives and property to rulers and soldiers and rely on the walls and fortifications of cities… Generation after generation is raised in such a condition until they come to resemble women and children, who are dependent on the head of the household.
But the Bedouins are their own guardians, always carrying weapons, relying on their own strength, and courage has become for them a trait and a nature."
@sahandiranmehr
